353752.title: Mirror invariance conjecture for the Thue–Morse two-block language
353752.statement: Let $x^{(00)}$ be the fixed point of the Thue–Morse two-block substitution, and let $L_{\rm\sc TM}$ be the language of all finite words occurring in $x^{(00)}$. A set of binary words is **mirror invariant** if, whenever it contains $w_1\dots w_m$, it also contains $(1-w_1)\dots(1-w_m)$. **Mirror invariance conjecture.** The language $L_{\rm\sc TM}$ is mirror invariant. This is contrasted with the fact that the language is not reversal invariant; proving mirror invariance is difficult because mirror images of occurring words may first appear only after many substitution iterations.

354088.title: Balanced max-part conjecture for K_4-free graphs
354088.statement:
Let $n$ be even and let $G$ be a $K_4$-free graph on $n$ vertices. A balanced $2$-partition is a partition $V(G)=A\cup B$ with $|A|=|B|=n/2$. **Balanced max-part conjecture for K_4-free graphs.** There exists a balanced $2$-partition such that each class spans at most $n^2/16$ edges:

$$
\max\{e(A),e(B)\}\leq n^2/16.
$$
 The bound is sharp for the complete 3-partite graph with class sizes $n/2,n/4,n/4$, and the conjecture is proved in the source for 3-partite graphs but remains open in general.

357228.title: Rall's Hamiltonian-path conjecture for the domination game
357228.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. A **Hamiltonian path** is a path containing every vertex of $G$ exactly once. The game domination number $\gamma_g(G)$ is the number of moves in the domination game when Dominator starts and both players play optimally. **Rall's conjecture.** If $G$ has a Hamiltonian path, then

$$
\gamma_g(G) \leq \left\lceil \frac{1}{2}n \right\rceil.
$$

The paper proves the weaker bound $\lceil 10n/17\rceil$ for graphs with a Hamiltonian path. Thus the conjectured half-order bound remains open.

358510.title: Workshop characterization conjecture for generically universally rigid graphs on the line
358510.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on at least three vertices. A graph is **generically universally rigid** in $\mathbb{R}^1$ if every one-dimensional generic framework of it is universally rigid.

**Workshop characterization conjecture.** The graph $G$ is generically universally rigid in $\mathbb{R}^1$ if and only if it can be obtained from a set of triangles by edge reduced attachment and edge addition operations.

358735.title: The stronger-than relation conjecture for graphs without semi-edges
358735.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be connected graphs. Write $A\triangleright B$ when every simple graph that covers $A$ also covers $B$, and write $A\longrightarrow B$ when $A$ covers $B$. A graph has no semi-edges if none of its edges is a semi-edge.

**The stronger-than relation conjecture.** If $A$ has no semi-edges, then

$$
A\triangleright B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\longrightarrow B.
$$

This conjecture characterizes the stronger-than relation for graphs without semi-edges and would show that the apparently broader relation yields no additional comparisons in that case. It was formulated as an open conjecture in the GROW 2022 open problem session.

362030.title: Short-distance inversion conjecture for even permutations
362030.statement:

364805.title: The exact hexagon-count conjecture for strongly regular graphs with parameters $\lambda=1$ and $\mu=2$
364805.statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly regular graph with parameters $\lambda=1$ and $\mu=2$, order $n$, and valency $k$. Let $p_6$ denote the number of hexagons in $G$. **Exact hexagon-count conjecture.** The number of hexagons in $G$ is equal to

$$
p_6=\frac{1}{12}nk(k-2)(2k^2-21k+53).
$$

The paper proves the same expression as a lower bound. Equality holds when the auxiliary quantity $n_3$ is zero; this condition means that two triangles connected through two edges are necessarily connected through the third edge. The conjecture is motivated by the claim that otherwise many symmetries are broken. Under this equality condition, Makhnev proved that $srg(99,14,1,2)$ does not exist.

365075.title: Mao, Wang, Magnant, and Schiermeyer's Gallai-Ramsey conjecture for the fan $F_3$
365075.statement:
A fan $F_n$ is the graph obtained by joining a new central vertex to every vertex of a matching of size $n$, and $GR_k(F_3)$ is its $k$-color Gallai-Ramsey number.

$$
GR_k(F_3)=

14\cdot5^{(k-2)/2}-1, & \text{if } k \text{ is even};\\
33\cdot5^{(k-3)/2}, & \text{if } k \text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

The paper supplies a new lower bound that exceeds the conjectured value for even $k$, so this conjecture is disproved.

365896.title: Exceptional sets for four ternary quadratic forms
365896.statement:
Let $\mathbb N$ denote the nonnegative integers and let $x,y,z\in\mathbb Z$. **Exceptional-set conjecture.** The following representation sets are exactly:

$$
\left\{\frac{x(5x+1)}2+\frac{y(5y+1)}2+\frac{z(5z+1)}2:x,y,z\in\mathbb Z\right\}=\mathbb N\setminus\{1,10,19,94\},
$$

$$
\left\{x(5x+1)+\frac{y(5y+1)}2+\frac{3z(5z+1)}2:x,y,z\in\mathbb Z\right\}=\mathbb N\setminus\{1,5,32\},
$$

$$
\left\{x(5x+1)+2y(5y+1)+\frac{z(5z+1)}2:x,y,z\in\mathbb Z\right\}=\mathbb N\setminus\{1,5,70\},
$$

$$
\left\{x(5x+1)+\frac{y(5y+1)}2+\frac{5z(5z+1)}2:x,y,z\in\mathbb Z\right\}=\mathbb N\setminus\{1,5\}.
$$

These claims give precise finite exceptional sets for four ternary quadratic representations. They are posed as conjectures after related corollaries, and the source supplies no resolution.

366233.title: Trivariate symmetries on vincular patterns
366233.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and define

$$
P_n(p,q,r,s)=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_n}p^{(\textrm{13--2})(\sigma)}q^{(\textrm{31--2})(\sigma)}r^{(\textrm{2--13})(\sigma)}s^{(\textrm{2--31})(\sigma)}.
$$

Here $(\textrm{13--2})$, $(\textrm{31--2})$, $(\textrm{2--13})$, and $(\textrm{2--31})$ denote the corresponding vincular-pattern statistics. **Trivariate symmetries on vincular patterns.** The following identities hold:

$$
P_n(1,q,r,s)=P_n(1,q,s,r),
$$

$$
P_n(p,1,r,s)=P_n(p,1,s,r),
$$

$$
P_n(p,q,1,s)=P_n(q,p,1,s),
$$

$$
P_n(p,q,r,1)=P_n(q,p,r,1).
$$

These identities extend the complementation and reversal symmetries of the four-variable polynomial $P_n$; their general validity beyond the stated empirical evidence remains open.

382304.title: Polynomial formulas for Betti numbers of squared-path cut complexes
382304.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, let $P_n^2$ denote its square, and let $\beta(k,n)$ be the unique nonzero Betti number of the cut complex $\Delta_k(P_n^2)$. 

**Polynomial formula conjecture.** For $k=4$ and $k=5$, the Betti numbers are conjectured to satisfy

$$
\beta(4,n)=3+8\binom{n-7}{1}+6\binom{n-7}{2}+\binom{n-7}{3},\qquad n\ge 7,
$$

$$
\beta(5,n)=6+20\binom{n-8}{1}+21\binom{n-8}{2}+7\binom{n-8}{3}+\binom{n-8}{4},\qquad n\ge 8.
$$

These formulas extend the computed Betti-number data for the squared path; no proof or resolution is supplied here.

382314.title: Minimal-order conjecture for graphs with large attacking-cop-number gap
382314.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $\operatorname{c}(H)$ and $\operatorname{cc}(H)$ denote its cop number and attacking cop number, respectively.

**Minimal-order conjecture for the attacking-cop-number gap.** If

$$
\operatorname{cc}(H)-\operatorname{c}(H)\geq k,
$$

then, for $k=2$, $n\geq 15$, while for $k=3$, $n\geq 58$.

This conjecture asserts that the known constructions with attacking cop number exceeding the cop number by two or three have minimal possible order. The source presents it as a conjecture about the minimality of the known examples.

382314.source_review: Source Conjecture 5.7 concerns gap at least 2 or 3. Source prints line graph of Petersen at order15 and seventeen order58 examples. Source Theorem 4.2 constructions cannot be shortened by a routine augmentation for credit.
382314.mathematical_attempt_and_coverage: No full attacking-game state enumeration completed. Standard bounds cc<=2c and cc<=domination_number rule out tiny connected examples through order7; that routine observation is not a solution. Report no exhaustive graph coverage beyond this.
382314.remaining_lemma_or_objection: Need an exact winning/losing game certificate at n<15 or n<58, or full lower bounds. Multi-cop state spaces and elimination of attacked cops require a faithful solver before search.
